attributes.probed_form: All 74 declared `extern [const] f32|f64|char lbl_8034xxxx;` in src/game/enemy/enemy.c inside 0x80346810..0x80346A70 were deleted and each of their 323 reference sites replaced by the shortest plain decimal (or C string) literal that round-trips to the datum's exact bytes read from orig/GUNE5D/sys/main.dol -- e.g. `lbl_80346840` -> `3.141592654`, `lbl_80346820` -> `0.0f`, `lbl_80346A38` -> `"GARG%s"`, negatives parenthesised as `(-3.141592654)`. Two sites additionally required the `*(volatile T*)&lbl_X` load scaffold to be dropped (`f32 zero = *(volatile f32*)&lbl_80346820;` -> `f32 zero = 0.0f;` at enemy.c:1567 and `(f64)amount < *(volatile f64*)&lbl_80346810` -> `(f64)amount < 1.0` at enemy.c:6698), because `&literal` is not an lvalue and the compile fails outright. A second variant HELD EVERYTHING FIXED EXCEPT lbl_80346820 (0.0f, 39 sites), to test whether the single non-const 39-site constant was the driver: it was not -- 11 functions still moved instead of 12. Everything was reverted; the tree is at HEAD for both TUs plus one unrelated committed keep.

The 15 addresses gamemain also references (0x80346810 0x80346820 0x80346830 0x80346840 0x80346848 0x80346850 0x80346868 0x80346870 0x803468B0 0x803468B8 0x803468F0 0x80346984 0x803469D4 0x80346A28 0x80346A30) are exactly WV's 15 -- CONFIRMED, not refuted. (2) WV's `gamemain.c additionally references TWENTY-FOUR symbols in the SAME run beyond enemy.c's span (lbl_80346A70 through lbl_80346AFC)` is a 3.7x UNDERCOUNT: measured at HEAD, gamemain references EIGHTY-NINE addresses above the enemy run, spanning 0x80346A70..0x80346CB4 (0x244 bytes, not 0x8C), and 16 of those addresses are ALSO referenced by game/world/gauntworld.c, which no record mentions -- a THIRD TU is entangled in the same run. (3) THE GAMEMAIN RUN IS TWO TUs, not one: see claim.PJ_the-gamemain-sdata2-run-splits-at-0x80346be0. (4) The enemy claim additionally needs the string block below 0x80346810 (0x80346704..0x80346808, the enemy-name strings SPIDER/MAGGOT/ZOMBIE/... which gamemain, not enemy, currently references), since a TU's section is contiguous. The price is twelve functions of matching work, six of them currently byte-exact and one (do_enemy_collide) whose behaviour chains the graph records as off-limits.

attributes.verification: THE POOL IS FULLY DECODED, which no prior record achieved. The enemy run is 0x80346810..0x80346A70 (0x260 bytes, 87 datums). All 34 anonymous pool entries our object already emits were matched to a UNIQUE target address by value: 21 of them to addresses no source reference names, and the 13 that no lbl_ symbol covers land EXACTLY in the eight unreferenced holes (0x80346828 0.001, 0x803468C0 0.005555555555555556, 0x803468C8 999999.0f, 0x803468D0 4503599627370496.0, 0x803468E8 3.106686068955556, 0x80346910 0.9, 0x80346950 -10.0, 0x80346958 0.6, 0x80346960 0.800000011920929f, 0x80346978 25.0, 0x80346990 18.0, 0x80346998 16.0, 0x803469A8 7.5). So OUR POOL CONTENT IS ENTIRELY CORRECT and the section is only under-emitted -- WV's and EO's diagnosis is confirmed at datum granularity. ORDER: a reloc-first-use model predicts the merged post-conversion order with only 7 inversions in 87 datums, 2 of which are bookkeeping artifacts (values whose target address is not unique) and 4 of which are adjacent-pair swaps 12-20 bytes apart in .text; the one genuine ordering defect is f64 3.0, whose first use in our source is at .text +0x5afe while the target places it at 0x803468B8, before the datum whose first use is +0x2822. THE BLOCKER IS NOT ORDER. `pj_ab_body` (scratch; builds the un-postprocessed body object from HEAD and from the converted source and compares instruction words per function) reports 12 of 66 functions with differing words: closest_enemy, do_enemy_move, do_enemy_collide, fn_80045C30, fn_8004646C, fn_8004DC2C, find_enemy_slot (frame growth of 8-24 bytes plus save-set shifts), move_logic06, move_logic14, damage_enemy, fn_8004DC2C (a pool load scheduled ahead of a struct load, register roles swapped), fn_8004DF58 (`fmul f31,f31,f0` -> `fmul f31,f0,f31`, a commutative operand swap) and move_logic22 (FPR recolor). Against the TARGET the same comparison gives raw differing words 968 -> 1102 (+134) and functions at zero differing words 45 -> 39; only move_logic22 improves (-23). `t16_rederive_body --apply` over all 13 pins: 9 UNCHANGED, move_logic22 BODY-MOVED and move_logic00 WINDOW-MOVED both re-derived BYTE-EQUAL, and 4 REFUSED by the rule's own guards with `non-register instruction bits differ` (damage_enemy +0x15c, fn_8004646C +0x8, closest_enemy +0x8, move_logic14 +0x1f0) -- the refusals are the guards correctly reporting the .text regression above, not renumber damage. After the revert: `ninja -j2` -> `build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK`, retail sha1 7cba77aa496eb0fc5ffec60efd9680aa9635d679, `defake_gate.py check game/enemy/enemy.c` GATE OK, STRICT 57.20% (2594 fns) + EQUIVALENT 11.92% (156 fns) -- identical to the baseline anchored at 84f85a96a, source sha1 3effb8e8d.

hypothesis.statement: The enemy .sdata2 claim is reachable only by ALSO closing the 12 functions the conversion moves. Nine of them are one mechanism -- an extern scalar read is an opaque reload the allocator must respect, a literal is rematerialisable -- so the next lane should try restoring the reload barrier WITHOUT the extern: a file-local `static const f64` per hostile constant, whose datum MWCC places after the anonymous literals (the winglobals `literals then const objects` pool law) and which therefore cannot sit at the target's address. If that ordering is fatal, the remaining lever is per-function source work on the seven frame-growth functions.
